title: The Broken Charger
story:
Lina's phone battery was almost empty on the afternoon train. She needed a map to find her uncle's new flat, so she took her charger from her bag. The cable looked fine, but the small metal plug was loose. She pushed it into the socket under the seat, yet nothing happened. The screen still showed a red battery icon.

A passenger across the aisle pointed to another socket beside the window. Lina tried again. The phone beeped, and a tiny lightning sign appeared. She felt relief. The journey would take forty minutes, which was enough time to add a little power.

Then the train stopped between two stations. The lights went off, and the socket stopped working too. The phone was only at twelve percent. Lina switched on flight mode so the battery would last longer. She copied her uncle's address onto paper, in case the phone went dark before she arrived.

When the lights returned, the socket worked again. The number climbed slowly to twenty percent. At the station she opened the map and walked for eight minutes to a blue door. Her uncle laughed at the broken charger. He kept a spare cable in a kitchen drawer and let her use it while they ate. Lina decided to buy a new charger the next morning, before another trip left her without a map.
